title: Peregrine SE implementation logbook
content:
Context: Peregrine Health — HIPAA customer evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for inference of clinical summarization model. SE kickoff 2026-02-28. This logbook is my personal running notes: meeting captures, config ideas, quick CLI snippets, and day-to-day todo items. Not a final artifact; intended for Marcus/Priya sync and handoff.

Key constraints / customer asks:
- Data must not leave customer VPC (no egress to hosted endpoints).
- HSM/KMS integration required for model keys and audit.
- Target p95 latency <= 250ms for 512-token summaries, burst to 1000 QPS during morning windows.
- Can start with single-model deployment (Llama-mimic-3b quantized) but want a plan for scaling to 13B family.

Meeting notes (2026-02-28, 14:00 PST) w/ Peregrine infra + security:
- Peregrine infra: AWS accounts (prod/staging), central transit VPC with AWS Transit Gateway. They prefer VPC peering + route tables for Private control plane connectivity.
- Security: HSM vendor = Thales Luna (customer-managed). KMS for S3 envelope keys. Audit retention requirements: 7 years.
- Observability: they want token-level cost breakdown (for chargeback) and per-request provenance headers.
- Questions raised: IP allowlist for control-plane, whether we run control-plane in their account or edge-proxy, telemetry retention in Private.

Decisions from meeting:
- Redwood will deploy the inference runtime into customer AWS account (Private) using the on-prem package and CloudFormation/Terraform modules.
- Use a control-plane connector (edge-proxy) in their transit VPC to minimize cross-account routing complexity.
- Initial model will be quantized 4-bit (GPTQ-like) on g5.8x or g4dn.12x for cost testing. For 13B fallback we propose g5.12x or A10G.

Open/Action items (personal tracker):
- [ ] SE-4721: Draft terraform module variant for transit-VPC edge-proxy (owner: Marcus).
- [x] Confirmed KMS integration approach with Peregrine security (contact: Claire Y.).
- [ ] Run perf estimate for 512 tokens on 3B q4: need p95 token latency simulation + cost/1M tokens. (owner: Elena)
- [ ] Prepare demo deploy script with sample deploy config and minimal infra (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Define canary rollout policy for model upgrades (A/B + auto-fallback).
- [ ] Capture network ACLs and expected ports (list below) and validate with Peregrine network team.

Quick network checklist (to send to customer network team):
- Outbound to Redwood control-plane IPs: TCP 443 (HTTPS) — only from edge-proxy in transit VPC.
- Inbound from customer apis to inference nodes: LB + port 8080 (http2) internally only.
- NFS/S3 access for model layer: VPC endpoint to S3 (no public access).
- HSM connectivity: TLS to Thales endpoints over port 1792 (as their vendor docs say) — confirm with Peregrine.

Sample minimal deploy config (notes / quick JSON for internal copy-paste)
- this is rough, not final:
{
  "deployment_name": "peregrine-summaries-v1",
  "model": "llama-mimic-3b-q4f16",
  "instance_type": "g5.8x",
  "replicas": 2,
  "max_batch_size": 16,
  "kv_cache": {"enabled": true, "max_prefix_bytes": 64},
  "rollback_policy": "auto-fallback: smaller-model"
}

Notes to self on KV cache and batching:
- Enable KV cache for conversational workloads. For summarization (single-turn large prompts) cache helps if prefix repeated (e.g., system prompt). For Peregrine we'll enable with conservative limits: 64KB per shard.
- Batching: p95 requirement pushes towards batch size <= 16 for 512 tokens on g5.8x. Start with suggested batch_size=8 and test under synthetic load.

Performance estimation stub (raw notes):
- 3B q4 model on g5.8x: rough throughput 160-220 tokens/s depending on kernel path. p95 latency for 512 tokens ~ 230-320ms (need run).
- 13B model on g5.12x: throughput ~ 65-90 tokens/s. p95 for 512 tokens likely >500ms unless we increase replica count / smaller batch.

Commands I used during POC (save for repeat):
- terraform plan: terraform -chdir=infra/peregrine apply -var-file=prod.tfvars
- runtime health check: curl -H "Accept: application/json" http://<node-ip>:8080/v1/health
- simple inference call (local): curl -X POST http://<edge-proxy>/v1/generate -d "{\"model\":\"llama-mimic-3b-q4f16\",\"inputs\":\"Summarize: patient note...\"}" -H "Content-Type: application/json"

Customer clarifying questions to follow up with:
- Are we okay with the edge-proxy pattern (they wanted full control but also minimal routing changes)? I think yes but get written sign-off.
- Audit logs: do they want push to their SIEM or an S3 bucket in their account? Offer both options.
- SLA/RPO: they asked about downtime window during upgrades. Need to provide a canary + traffic-shift doc.

Personal timeline + next two weeks plan (rough):
- Mar 1–3: perf runs for 3B q4 on g5.8x; produce p50/p95/p99 table.
- Mar 4–6: infra terraform for transit-VPC edge-proxy module; internal review.
- Mar 8: send network ACL checklist and sample deploy config to Peregrine network team.
- Mar 9–12: demo deploy in staging with small dataset (Priya to run deploy).
- Mar 13: sync w/ Marcus and handoff for production cutover planning.

Random notes / heuristics I want to remember:
- For HSM integration, recommend envelope encryption: customer KMS -> envelope key -> model artifacts in S3. Avoid passing private keys to runtime.
- For high QPS bursts, use short-lived pre-warmed replicas + autoscale policy that allows immediate burst capacity (we implement this as reserve_count + burst_queue).

Meeting transcript highlights (abridged):
- Peregrine security: "We cannot accept any model weights on a hosted account. All artifacts must be in our S3 or our HSM-decrypted ephemeral space."
- Marcus: "Let's keep first deploy minimal: 2 replicas, quantized 3B, validate latencies, then iterate."

Log (quick entries):
- 2026-03-02 09:15 — kicked off perf run (3B q4). Noticed outlier p99 spikes around 2x median when GC interleaves (need deeper runtime trace).
- 2026-03-04 16:30 — terraform module skeleton committed (ops PR link above). Still needs IAM boundary review.

Questions for Marcus/Priya before I pass to AE/Customer:
1) Acceptable retention for runtime traces? (we propose 30 days, they can request longer for audit).
2) Do we prepare two deployment templates (single-replica quickstart + prod multi-replica)? I think yes.
3) Is there a firm date for the 13B migration or just a future goal? If concrete, we need GPU sku reservation.

Quick todo ping template to send Peregrine (short email body):
- Subject: Redwood Private - next infra items for VPC peering
- Body (bullets): confirm CIDR blocks, confirm HSM endpoints and port, provide public keys for control-plane allowlist, preferred staging window for deploy (2–4hrs).

End of logbook entry. Save and iterate.

Notes to self: keep this file as ephemeral; once we stabilize the design I'll move canonical instructions to Confluence page and the terraform to infra repo.

-- Elena
